EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY: This go-to-market recommendation evaluates the introduction of a 65W GaN charger into the Vietnamese ecommerce market. Grounded strictly in evidence from technical documentation, Vietnamese tech forums (Tinhte, VOZ), and Shopee competitor observations, the strategy focuses on capturing urban office workers and tech commuters burdened by heavy OEM chargers. Because financial baselines (CAC, LTV, ROAS, budgets) and specific product details (port count, pricing, protocols, cables) are entirely unknown, execution requires a phased, evidence-controlled approach. All live public distribution is strictly subject to human approval under SUPERVISED autonomy.

RESEARCH_FINDINGS.summary: GaN power semiconductors enable higher power efficiency, higher switching frequencies, and significantly smaller form factors compared to legacy silicon MOSFETs.
65W USB-C Power Delivery can charge typical 13-inch and 14-inch ultrabooks and fast-charging smartphones through universal Type-C negotiation.
Vietnamese office workers and tech commuters express frustration carrying heavy OEM brick chargers and worry about thermal heat dissipation and wall socket plug stability.

Shopee Vietnam search discovery reveals competitor brands (Baseus, Ugreen, Anker) priced between 300,000 VND and 700,000 VND, with customers valuing port versatility, fast laptop handshake, and compact travel size.
Vietnamese tech forum users voice strong fear of cheap knockoffs causing voltage surges or frying expensive laptop motherboards, demanding clear safety and warranty.

KNOWN_FACTS: Competitor products in Vietnam (Baseus, Ugreen, Anker) trade in the 300,000 VND to 700,000 VND price range on Shopee
Vietnamese commuters and office workers frequently carry heavy OEM chargers
OBSERVATIONS: Tech forum users on Tinhte and VOZ actively discuss the burden of heavy adapter bricks and the desire for single-adapter travel convenience for laptops and phones.
Shopee buyers heavily evaluate port versatility and fast laptop handshakes when purchasing chargers.
Consumer anxiety regarding motherboard damage from unverified power supplies is a dominant sentiment in Vietnamese tech communities.
INFERENCES: Target customers in Vietnam seek relief from backpack weight when commuting between home and office.
Trust and safety assurance are paramount prerequisites for non-OEM charger adoption given widespread fear of hardware damage.
Competitive positioning must address reliability and safety to overcome consumer skepticism against unknown or new brands.
HYPOTHESES: If we position the compact form factor around backpack weight reduction for urban commuters, then initial consideration will increase among mobile office workers.
If we explicitly address safety and quality standards in our messaging, then consumer hesitation regarding non-OEM hardware damage will decrease.
UNKNOWNS: Exact number of ports (single vs multi-port is UNKNOWN/TO_BE_DETERMINED)
